title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 107 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued / The Lover and the Beloved begins
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 552–556 (Night 107, continuing directly from nights-106), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 107 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. At nightfall Ḍawʾ al-Makān asks the vizier Dandān for the story he promised, and Dandān begins a tale within the tale: the story of a lover, his beloved and the go-between who spoke for them. It opens with Sulaymān Shāh, a generous king of the Green City beyond the mountains of Isfahan, who has neither wife nor child. His vizier will not advise a king on what lies in God's hands, and tells him to buy a slave girl; the king refuses a concubine of unknown birth and asks instead for a princess of known lineage. The vizier praises the daughter of King Zahrshāh of the White Land, in prose and in verse, and is sent with a great train of gifts to ask for her hand. The night ends as he stands before Zahrshāh's jewelled throne and begins to speak. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ السَّابِعَةُ بَعْدَ الْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-sābiʿatu baʿda al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the seventh after the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundred and seventh night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ الْمَلِكَ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ لَمَّا أَحْضَرَ الْوَزِيرَ وَالْحَاجِبَ وَرُسْتُمَ وَبَهْرَامَ الْتَفَتَ إِلَى الْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-malika ḍawʾa al-makāni lammā aḥḍara al-wazīra wa-al-ḥājiba wa-rustuma wa-bahrāma iltafata ilā al-wazīri dandāna
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that King Ḍawʾ al-Makān, when he had brought the vizier and the chamberlain and Rustam and Bahrām, turned to the vizier Dandān
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when King Ḍawʾ al-Makān had summoned the vizier, the chamberlain, Rustam and Bahrām, he turned to the vizier Dandān
sentences.n: Shahrazād takes up the night by repeating, almost word for word, the scene that closed the last one. The print runs al-saʿīd and anna together, as it often does.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ اعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْوَزِيرُ أَنَّ اللَّيْلَ قَدْ أَقْبَلَ وَسَدَلَ جَلَابِيبَهُ عَلَيْنَا وَأَسْبَلَ وَنُرِيدُأَنْ تَحْكِيَ لَنَا مَا وَعَدْتَنَا بِهِ مِنَ الْحِكَايَاتِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla iʿlam ayyuhā al-wazīru anna al-layla qad aqbala wa-sadala jalābībahu ʿalaynā wa-asbala wa-nurīdu an taḥkiya lanā mā waʿadtanā bihi mina al-ḥikāyāti
sentences.l: and said: Know, O vizier, that the night has come-on, and has drawn its mantles down over us and let (them) fall; and we wish that you tell us what you promised us of the tales.
sentences.i: and said, “Know, O vizier, that night has come and drawn its cloaks down over us; we would have you tell us the tales you promised.”
sentences.n: The print has نحكي, “that we tell”, a misprint for تحكي, “that you tell”, corrected here. It also runs nurīdu and an together. Rhymed prose: aqbala / asbala.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ حُبًّا وَكَرَامَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru ḥubban wa-karāmatan
sentences.l: And the vizier said: With love and honour.
sentences.i: “Gladly, and with all my heart,” said the vizier.

sentences.t: اعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّهُ بَلَغَنِي مِنْ حِكَايَةِ الْعَاشِقِ وَالْمَعْشُوقِ وَالْمُتَكَلِّمِ بَيْنَهُمَا وَمَاجَرَى لَهُمْ مِنَ الْعَجَائِبِ وَالْغَرَائِبِ مَايُزِيلُ الْهَمَّ عَنِ الْقُلُوبِ وَيُسَلِّي عَنْ مِثْلِ حُزْنِ يَعْقُوبَ
sentences.tr: iʿlam ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu annahu balaghanī min ḥikāyati al-ʿāshiqi wa-al-maʿshūqi wa-al-mutakallimi baynahumā wa-mā jarā lahum mina al-ʿajāʾibi wa-al-gharāʾibi mā yuzīlu al-hamma ʿani al-qulūbi wa-yusallī ʿan mithli ḥuzni yaʿqūba
sentences.l: Know, O king the happy, that there has reached me, of the tale of the lover and the beloved and the one-who-spoke between the two of them, and what befell them of wonders and marvels, what removes care from hearts and consoles for (a grief) like the grief of Jacob.
sentences.i: “Know, O fortunate king, that I have heard a tale of a lover and his beloved, and of the one who spoke for them between them, and of the wonders and marvels that befell them: a tale to lift care from the heart and console even a grief like Jacob's.
sentences.n: The print has والمنكلم, a misprint for والمتكلم (al-mutakallim, “the one who speaks”, here the go-between), corrected here. Rhymed prose: al-qulūb / yaʿqūb. Jacob's grief is his mourning for his lost son Joseph, the byword for inconsolable sorrow. The print runs together al-saʿīd and annahu, wa- and mā jarā, and mā and yuzīlu.

sentences.t: وَهُوَأَنَّهُ كَانَ فِي سَالِفِ الزَّمَانِ مَدِينَةٌ وَرَاءَ جِبَالِ أَصْبَهَانَ يُقَالُ لَهَا الْمَدِينَةُ الْخَضْرَاءُ
sentences.tr: wa-huwa annahu kāna fī sālifi al-zamāni madīnatun warāʾa jibāli aṣbahāna yuqālu lahā al-madīnatu al-khaḍrāʾu
sentences.l: And it is that there was in bygone time a city behind the mountains of Iṣbahān, it-was-said to it the City the Green.
sentences.i: It is this. In days gone by there was a city beyond the mountains of Iṣbahān called the Green City.
sentences.n: wa-huwa annahu, “and it is that …”, is the storyteller's turn from promise to tale; the print runs the words together. Iṣbahān is Isfahan in Persia; a few lines on the text spells it Iṣfahān.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ بِهَا مَلِكٌ يُقَالُ لَهُ الْمَلِكُ سُلَيْمَانُ شَاهْ وَكَانَ صَاحِبَ جُودٍ وَإِحْسَانٍ وَعَدْلٍ وَأَمَانٍ وَفَضْلٍ وَامْتِنَانٍ وَسَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ الرُّكْبَانُ مِنْ كُلِّ مَكَانٍ وَشَاعَ ذِكْرُهُ فِى سَائِرِ الْأَقْطَارِ وَالْبُلْدَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna bihā malikun yuqālu lahu al-maliku sulaymānu shāh wa-kāna ṣāḥiba jūdin wa-iḥsānin wa-ʿadlin wa-amānin wa-faḍlin wa-imtinānin wa-sārat ilayhi al-rukbānu min kulli makānin wa-shāʿa dhikruhu fī sāʾiri al-aqṭāri wa-al-buldāni
sentences.l: And there was in it a king, it-was-said to him King Sulaymān Shāh, and he was a possessor of generosity and beneficence, and justice and safety, and bounty and favour; and the riders journeyed to him from every place, and his mention spread in all the regions and the lands.
sentences.i: In it there reigned a king called Sulaymān Shāh, a man of generosity and kindness, of justice and security, of bounty and grace. Riders came to him from every quarter, and his fame spread through every region and land.
sentences.n: The print has يقال لها, “called (she)”, a misprint for يقال له, “called (he)”, corrected here: the slip repeats the يقال لها of the city just before. The sajʿ runs on one rhyme: iḥsān, amān, imtinān, rukbān, makān, buldān.

sentences.t: وَأَقَامَ فِى الْمَمْلَكَةِ مُدَّةً مَدِيدَةً مِنَ الزَّمَانِ وَهُوَ فِى عِزٍّ وَأَمَانٍ إِلَّا أَنَّهُ كَانَ خَالِيًا مِنَ الْأَوْلَادِ وَالزَّوْجَاتِ
sentences.tr: wa-aqāma fī al-mamlakati muddatan madīdatan mina al-zamāni wa-huwa fī ʿizzin wa-amānin illā annahu kāna khāliyan mina al-awlādi wa-al-zawjāti
sentences.l: And he stayed in the kingdom a period long of time, and he (was) in might and safety, except that he was empty of children and wives.
sentences.i: He ruled the kingdom for a long while in power and security, save that he had neither children nor wives.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ لَهُ وَزِيرٌ يُقَارِبُهُ فِى الصِّفَاتِ مِنَ الْجُودِ وَالْهِبَاتِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna lahu wazīrun yuqāribuhu fī al-ṣifāti mina al-jūdi wa-al-hibāti
sentences.l: And there was to him a vizier who came-near him in the qualities, of generosity and gifts.
sentences.i: He had a vizier who came close to him in his virtues of generosity and giving.

sentences.t: فَاتَّفَقَ أَنَّهُ أَرْسَلَ إِلَى وَزِيرِهِ يَوْمًا مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ وَأَحْضَرَهُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ittafaqa annahu arsala ilā wazīrihi yawman mina al-ayyāmi wa-aḥḍarahu bayna yadayhi
sentences.l: And it happened that he sent to his vizier one day of the days and brought him between his two hands,
sentences.i: It happened one day that he sent for his vizier and had him brought before him,

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا وَزِيرِي إِنَّهُ قَدْ ضَاقَ صَدْرِي وَعِيلَ صَبْرِى وَضَعُفَ مِنِّي الْجَلَدُ لِكَوْنِي بِلَا زَوْجَةٍ وَلَا وَلَدٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahu yā wazīrī innahu qad ḍāqa ṣadrī wa-ʿīla ṣabrī wa-ḍaʿufa minnī al-jaladu li-kawnī bi-lā zawjatin wa-lā waladin
sentences.l: and said to him: O my vizier, it is that my breast has grown-narrow, and my patience has been exhausted, and the endurance has weakened from me, for my being without wife and without child.
sentences.i: and said to him, “O my vizier, my heart is heavy, my patience is spent and my strength fails me, because I have neither wife nor child.
sentences.n: ḍāqa ṣadrī, “my breast grew narrow”, is the usual idiom for distress; ʿīla ṣabrī, “my patience was overcome”. Rhymed: ṣadrī / ṣabrī.

sentences.t: وَمَا هَذَا سَبِيلُ الْمُلُوكِ الْحُكَّامِ عَلَى كُلِّ أَمِيرٍ وَصُعْلُوكٍ فَإِنَّهُمْ يَفْرَحُونَ بِخِلْفَهِ الْأَوْلَادِ وَتَتَضَاعَفُ لَهُمْ بِهِمُ الْعَدَدُ وَالْأَعْدَادُ
sentences.tr: wa-mā hādhā sabīlu al-mulūki al-ḥukkāmi ʿalā kulli amīrin wa-ṣuʿlūkin fa-innahum yafraḥūna bi-khilfati al-awlādi wa-tataḍāʿafu lahum bihimu al-ʿadadu wa-al-aʿdādu
sentences.l: And this is not the way of the kings, the rulers over every emir and pauper; for they rejoice in the offspring of children, and there are doubled for them by them the number and the numbers.
sentences.i: This is not the way of kings who rule over every prince and pauper: they rejoice in a line of children, and by them their numbers are multiplied many times over.
sentences.n: khilfa is “offspring, succession”; the print writes it with ه for ة, as it often does, so bi-khilfati al-awlād is “in the succession of children”. al-ʿadad wa-al-aʿdād, “the number and the numbers”, is a jingle for increase; the feminine-looking verb tataḍāʿafu with a masculine subject is loose agreement.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ تَنَاكَحُوا تَنَاسَلُوا تَكْثُرُوا فَإِنِّي مُبَاهٍ بِكُمُ الْأُمَمَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla al-nabiyyu ṣallā allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallama tanākaḥū tanāsalū takthurū fa-innī mubāhin bikumu al-umama yawma al-qiyāmati
sentences.l: And the Prophet said, God bless him and give him peace: Marry-one-another, beget-one-another, (and) you will become many; for I (am) one-who-vies by you with the nations on the Day of the Resurrection.
sentences.i: And the Prophet, God bless him and give him peace, said: ‘Marry and have children, and you will multiply; for on the Day of Resurrection I shall boast of your numbers before the nations.’
sentences.n: The print has ثكثروا, a misprint for تكثروا (takthurū, “you will become many”, jussive in answer to the commands), corrected here. The saying is a well-known hadith. mubāhin is pointed in the print: “vying in glory through you” — the Prophet will pride himself on the size of his community.

sentences.t: فَمَا عِنْدَكَ مِنَ الرَّأْيِ يَا وَزِيرُ فَشِرْ عَلَيَّ بِمَا فِيهِ النُّصْحُ مِنَ التَّدْبِيرِ
sentences.tr: fa-mā ʿindaka mina al-raʾyi yā wazīru fa-shir ʿalayya bi-mā fīhi al-nuṣḥu mina al-tadbīri
sentences.l: So what (is) with you of opinion, O vizier? So advise upon me with what in it (is) the sincere-counsel of planning.
sentences.i: So what is your opinion, vizier? Advise me what course holds good counsel.”
sentences.n: fa-shir is the imperative of ashāra, “to advise”, with its hamza dropped (Classical ashir); ashāra ʿalā is “advise someone”, and bi- names the advice given.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْوَزِيرُ ذَلِكَ الْكَلَامَ فَاضَتِ الدُّمُوعُ مِنْ عَيْنِهِ بِالِانْسِجَامِ وَقَالَ لَهُ هَيْهَاتَ يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ أَنْ أَتَكَلَّمَ فِيمَا هُوَ مِنْ خَصَائِصِ الرَّحْمٰنِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-wazīru dhālika al-kalāma fāḍati al-dumūʿu min ʿaynihi bi-al-insijāmi wa-qāla lahu hayhāta yā malika al-zamāni an atakallama fīmā huwa min khaṣāʾiṣi al-raḥmāni
sentences.l: And when the vizier heard that speech, the tears overflowed from his eye in streaming, and he said to him: Far (be it), O king of the time, that I speak in what is of the special-preserves of the Merciful.
sentences.i: When the vizier heard this, tears streamed from his eyes, and he said, “Far be it from me, O king of the age, to speak of what belongs to the Merciful alone.
sentences.n: hayhāta, “far from it!”, refuses the request: whether a man is granted children is God's own affair, and the vizier will not presume to advise on it. Rhymed: al-zamān / al-raḥmān.

sentences.t: أَتُرِيدُأَنْ أَدْخُلَ النَّارَ بِسَخَطِ الْمَلِكِ الْجَبَّارِ فَاشْتَرِ جَارِيَةً
sentences.tr: a-turīdu an adkhula al-nāra bi-sakhaṭi al-maliki al-jabbāri fa-ishtari jāriyatan
sentences.l: Do you want that I enter the Fire through the wrath of the King the Mighty? So buy a slave-girl.
sentences.i: Do you want me to enter the Fire under the wrath of the Almighty King? Buy a slave girl.”
sentences.n: The print runs turīdu and an together. bi-, “through, by”: the wrath is what would send him there. al-malik al-jabbār, “the Mighty King”, is God.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْمَلِكُ اعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْوَزِيرُ أَنَّ الْمَلِكَ إِذَا اشْتَرَى جَارِيَةً لَايَعْلَمُ حَسَبَهَا وَلَا يَعْرِفُ نَسَبَهَا فَهُوَ لَايَدْرِي خَسَاسَةَ أَصْلِهَا حَتَّى يَجْتَنِبَهَا وَلَاشَرَفَ عُنْصُرِهَا حَتَّى يَتَسَرَّى بِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-maliku iʿlam ayyuhā al-wazīru anna al-malika idhā ishtarā jāriyatan lā yaʿlamu ḥasabahā wa-lā yaʿrifu nasabahā fa-huwa lā yadrī khasāsata aṣlihā ḥattā yajtanibahā wa-lā sharafa ʿunṣurihā ḥattā yatasarrā bihā
sentences.l: And the king said to him: Know, O vizier, that the king, when he buys a slave-girl, does not know her rank nor know her lineage; so he does not know the baseness of her root, so that he might avoid her, nor the nobility of her stock, so that he might take her as concubine.
sentences.i: The king said to him, “Know, vizier, that when a king buys a slave girl he knows neither her standing nor her lineage. He cannot tell whether her origin is base, so as to keep away from her, or her stock noble, so as to take her to his bed.
sentences.n: ḥasab is rank earned by one's forebears' deeds, nasab the line of descent: the rhymed pair covers all of a woman's “family”. tasarrā bi- is “take as a concubine (surriyya)”. The print runs lā together with the next word three times here.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا أَفْضَي إِلَيْهَا رُبَّمَا حَمَلَتْ مِنْهُ فَيَجِيءُ الْوَلَدُ مُنَافِقًا ظَالِمًا سَافِكًا لِلدِّمَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā afḍā ilayhā rubbamā ḥamalat minhu fa-yajīʾu al-waladu munāfiqan ẓāliman sāfikan li-al-dimāʾi
sentences.l: And when he goes-in to her, perhaps she conceives from him, and the child comes (out) a hypocrite, an oppressor, a shedder of blood.
sentences.i: And when he lies with her she may conceive by him, and the child will turn out a hypocrite, a tyrant, a shedder of blood.
sentences.n: afḍā ilā, literally “to reach, come through to”, is a decent phrase for lying with a woman. The print spells it with ي for final ى. li-, “of”: it marks the object of sāfik, “shedder”.

sentences.t: وَيَكُونُ مَثَلُهَا مَثَلَ الْأَرْضِ السَّبِخَةِ إِذَا زُرِعَ فِيهَا زَرْعٌ فَإِنَّهُ يَخْبُثُ نَبَاتُهُ وَلَايَحْسُنُ ثَبَاتُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-yakūnu mathaluhā mathala al-arḍi al-sabikhati idhā zuriʿa fīhā zarʿun fa-innahu yakhbuthu nabātuhu wa-lā yaḥsunu thabātuhu
sentences.l: And her likeness is the likeness of the salt-marshy ground: when a sowing is sown in it, its growth turns-bad and its firmness is not good.
sentences.i: She is like salt-marsh ground: sow seed in it and the shoots come up stunted and never take firm root.
sentences.n: Rhymed: nabātuhu / thabātuhu. The image is Qurʾanic in flavour: good land brings forth its plants, bad land only meanly.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ يَكُونُ ذَلِكَ الْوَلَدُ مُتَعَرِّضًا لِسَخَطِ مَوْلَاهُ وَلَا يَفْعَلُ مَا أَمَرَ بِهِ وَلَا يَجْتَنِبُ مَا عَنْهُ نَهَاهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qad yakūnu dhālika al-waladu mutaʿarriḍan li-sakhaṭi mawlāhu wa-lā yafʿalu mā amara bihi wa-lā yajtanibu mā ʿanhu nahāhu
sentences.l: And that child may be exposing-himself to the wrath of his Lord, and does not do what He commanded, nor avoid what He forbade him from.
sentences.i: Such a child may well bring down on himself the wrath of his Lord, doing nothing that He commands and shunning nothing that He forbids.
sentences.n: mawlāhu, “his master”, is God here. amara bi- is “command (something)”; the bi- marks the thing commanded. Rhymed: mawlāhu / nahāhu.

sentences.t: فَأَنَا لَا أَتَسَبَّبُ فِي هَذَا بِشِرَاءِ جَارِيَةٍ أَبَدًا وَإِنَّمَا مُرَادِي أَنْ تَخْطُبَ لِي بِنْتًا مِنْ بَنَاتِ الْمُلُوكِ يَكُونُ نَسَبُهَا مَعْرُوفًا وَجَمَالُهَا مَوْصُوفًا
sentences.tr: fa-anā lā atasabbabu fī hādhā bi-shirāʾi jāriyatin abadan wa-innamā murādī an takhṭuba lī bintan min banāti al-mulūki yakūnu nasabuhā maʿrūfan wa-jamāluhā mawṣūfan
sentences.l: So I will not make-means in this by the buying of a slave-girl, ever; rather my wish is that you ask-in-marriage for me a girl from the daughters of the kings, whose lineage is known and whose beauty is described.
sentences.i: So I will never go about this by buying a slave girl. What I want is for you to seek me in marriage a king's daughter, whose lineage is known and whose beauty is spoken of.
sentences.n: khaṭaba li-, “ask for (a woman's) hand on someone's behalf”. Rhymed: maʿrūfan / mawṣūfan.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ دَلَلْتَنِي عَلَى ذَاتِ النَّسَبِ وَالدِّينِ مِنْ بَنَاتِ الْمُلُوكِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَإِنِّي أَخْطُبُهَا وَأَتَزَوَّجُ بِهَا عَلَى رُؤُسِ الْأَشْهَادِ لِيَحْصُلَ لِي بِذَلِكَ رِضَاءُ رَبِّ الْعِبَادِ
sentences.tr: fa-in dalaltanī ʿalā dhāti al-nasabi wa-al-dīni min banāti al-mulūki al-muslimīna fa-innī akhṭubuhā wa-atazawwaju bihā ʿalā ruʾūsi al-ashhādi li-yaḥṣula lī bi-dhālika riḍāʾu rabbi al-ʿibādi
sentences.l: And if you guide me to one-possessing lineage and religion, of the daughters of the Muslim kings, then I will ask-for-her and marry her on the heads of the witnesses, so that there may be gained for me by that the good-pleasure of the Lord of the servants.
sentences.i: If you can show me a daughter of the Muslim kings who has both lineage and faith, I will ask for her hand and marry her before all witnesses, and so win the favour of the Lord of all His servants.”
sentences.n: ʿalā ruʾūs al-ashhād, “on the heads of the witnesses”, is “publicly, before everyone”. tazawwaja bi- is “marry (a woman)”: the verb takes its object with bi-. Rhymed: al-ashhād / al-ʿibād.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَزِيرُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَضَى حَاجَتَكَ وَبَلَّغَكَ أُمْنِيَّتَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-wazīru inna allāha qaḍā ḥājataka wa-ballaghaka umniyyataka
sentences.l: And the vizier said to him: God has fulfilled your need and brought you to your wish.
sentences.i: The vizier said, “God has granted what you need and brought you your heart's desire.
sentences.n: The perfect tense here is a wish that speaks as if already done: “God has granted …”, that is, “God grant …”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ اعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ أَنَّهُ بَلَغَنِي أَنَّ الْمَلِكَ زَهْرْشَاه صَاحِبَ الْأَرْضِ الْبَيْضَاءِ لَهُ بِنْتٌ بَارِعَةُ الْجَمَالِ يَعْجِزُ عَنْ وَصْفِهَا الْقِيلُ وَالْقَالُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu iʿlam ayyuhā al-maliku annahu balaghanī anna al-malika zahrshāh ṣāḥiba al-arḍi al-bayḍāʾi lahu bintun bāriʿatu al-jamāli yaʿjizu ʿan waṣfihā al-qīlu wa-al-qālu
sentences.l: And he said to him: Know, O king, that it has reached me that King Zahrshāh, lord of the White Land, has a daughter surpassing of beauty; there fails from describing her the said and the saying.
sentences.i: He said to him, “Know, O king, that I have heard that King Zahrshāh, lord of the White Land, has a daughter of surpassing beauty, beyond the power of any words to describe.
sentences.n: al-qīl wa-al-qāl, “what is said and the saying”, is all talk; here, all that could be said fails to describe her. The kasra on yaʿjizu is the print's.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يُوجَدْ لَهَا فِي هَذَا الزَّمَانِ مَثِيلٌ لِأَنَّهَا فِي غَايَةِ الْكَمَالِ قَوِيمَةُ الِاعْتِدَالِ ذَاتُ طَرْفٍ كَحِيلٍ وَشَعْرٍ طَوِيلٍ وَخَصْرٍ نَحِيلٍ وَرِدْفٍ ثَقِيلٍ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yūjad lahā fī hādhā al-zamāni mathīlun li-annahā fī ghāyati al-kamāli qawīmatu al-iʿtidāli dhātu ṭarfin kaḥīlin wa-shaʿrin ṭawīlin wa-khaṣrin naḥīlin wa-ridfin thaqīlin
sentences.l: And there has not been found for her in this time a like, because she (is) in the utmost of perfection, straight of proportion, possessor of a glance kohl-dark, and hair long, and waist slender, and hips heavy.
sentences.i: In this age her like is not to be found, for she is perfection itself, straight and well proportioned, with kohl-dark eyes, long hair, a slender waist and heavy hips.
sentences.n: The catalogue is the standard portrait of beauty in the Nights, in rhymed pairs: kaḥīl, ṭawīl, naḥīl, thaqīl. ṭarf is the glance, or the eye; kaḥīl, “as if lined with kohl”, is dark-rimmed by nature.

sentences.t: إِنْ أَقْبَلَتْ فَتَنَتْ وَإِنْ أَدْبَرَتْ قَتَلَتْ تَأْخُذُ الْقَلْبَ وَالنَّاظِرَ كَمَا قَالَ فِيهَا الشَّاعِرُ
sentences.tr: in aqbalat fatanat wa-in adbarat qatalat taʾkhudhu al-qalba wa-al-nāẓira kamā qāla fīhā al-shāʿiru
sentences.l: If she comes-forward she enchants, and if she turns-back she kills; she takes the heart and the eye, as the poet said of her:
sentences.i: Coming towards you she bewitches; turning away she slays; she captures heart and eye alike, as the poet said of her:
sentences.n: fatanat / qatalat: the twin verbs rhyme. al-nāẓir is “the one who looks”, or the pupil of the eye.

sentences.t:
هَيْفَاءُ تُخْجِلُ غُصْنَ الْبَانِ قَامَتُهَا * لَمْ يَحْكِ طَلْعَتَهَا شَمْسٌ وَلَا قَمَرُ
كَانَّمَا رِيقُهَا شَهْدٌ وَقَدْ مُزِجَتْ * بِهِ الْمُدَامَةُ لَكِنْ ثَغْرُهَا دُرَرُ
مَمْشُوقَةُ الْقَدِّ مِنْ حُورِ الْجِنَانِ لَهَا * وَجْهٌ جَمِيلٌ وَفِي اَلْحَاظِهَا حَوَرُ
وَكَمْ لَهَا مِنْ قَتِيلٍ مَاتَ مِنْ كَمَدٍ * وَفِي طَرِيقِ هَوَاهَا الْخَوْفُ وَالْخَطَرُ
اِنْ شِئْتُ فَهِيَ الْمُنَى مَا شِئْتَ اَذْكُرُهَا * اَوْ مُتُّ مِنْ دُونِهَا لَمْ يُجْلِ فِي الْعُمُرِ
sentences.tr:
hayfāʾu tukhjilu ghuṣna al-bāni qāmatuhā * lam yaḥki ṭalʿatahā shamsun wa-lā qamaru
ka-annamā rīquhā shahdun wa-qad muzijat * bihi al-mudāmatu lākin thaghruhā duraru
mamshūqatu al-qaddi min ḥūri al-jināni lahā * wajhun jamīlun wa-fī alḥāẓihā ḥawaru
wa-kam lahā min qatīlin māta min kamadin * wa-fī ṭarīqi hawāhā al-khawfu wa-al-khaṭaru
in shiʾtu fa-hiya al-munā mā shiʾta adhkuruhā * aw muttu min dūnihā lam yujli fī al-ʿumuri
sentences.l:
Slender-waisted, her stature shames the bough of the bān; neither sun nor moon has copied her rising-face.
As if her saliva (were) honey, and there has been mixed with it the wine; but her mouth (is) pearls.
Lithe of figure, of the houris of the gardens; she has a face beautiful, and in her glances (is) ḥawar.
And how many a slain one she has, who died of grief; and on the road of her love (lie) the fear and the danger.
If I wish, then she (is) the desire — whatever you wish — I mention her; or if I die short of her, (it) did not … in the lifetime.
sentences.i:
Slender, her figure puts the willow-bough to shame; no sun nor moon can match the rising of her face.
Her mouth's sweet dew is honey with wine mingled in it, and yet her teeth are pearls.
Lithe as a houri of Paradise, her face is lovely, and her glances dark and bright.
How many has she slain who died of grief! On the road to her love lie fear and peril.
If I will, she is all I long for, and I tell of her as you will; and if I die without her, no lifetime …
sentences.n: The verse is copied as the print points it. The bān is the slender moringa tree, the stock image of a graceful figure. ḥawar is the sharp contrast of white and black in the eye, the beauty of the ḥūr, the houris. The last line is obscure as printed: لم يُجْلِ does not give clear sense (perhaps for لم يُجْدِ, “it would have availed nothing”), and al-ʿumuri breaks the poem's -ru rhyme; it is translated only as far as the words allow.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ الْوَزِيرُ مِنْ وَصْفِ تِلْكَ الْجَارِيَةِ قَالَ لِلْمَلِكِ سُلَيْمَانَ شَاهْ الرَّأْى عِنْدِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ أَنْ تُرْسِلَ إِلَى أَبِيهَا رَسُولًا فَطِنًا خَبِيرًا بِالْأُمُورِ مُجَرَّبًا لِتَصَارِيفِ الدُّهُورِ لِيَتَلَطَّفَ فِي خِطْبَتِهَا لَكَ مِنْ أَبِيهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha al-wazīru min waṣfi tilka al-jāriyati qāla li-al-maliki sulaymāna shāh al-raʾyu ʿindī ayyuhā al-maliku an tursila ilā abīhā rasūlan faṭinan khabīran bi-al-umūri mujarraban li-taṣārīfi al-duhūri li-yatalaṭṭafa fī khiṭbatihā laka min abīhā
sentences.l: And when the vizier finished from the description of that girl, he said to King Sulaymān Shāh: The opinion with me, O king, (is) that you send to her father a messenger, shrewd, expert in the affairs, tried by the turns of the ages, that he may use-tact in asking for her for you from her father.
sentences.i: When the vizier had finished describing the girl he said to King Sulaymān Shāh, “My counsel, O king, is that you send her father an envoy who is shrewd, experienced in affairs and tried by the turns of fortune, to ask her father for her hand on your behalf with all due tact.
sentences.n: jāriya, “girl”, is used here of a free princess, not a slave. Rhymed: al-umūr / al-duhūr. li-, “by”: mujarrab li- is “tested by”.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهَا لَانَظِيرَ لَهَا فِي قَاصِي الْأَرْضِ وَدَانِيهَا وَتَحْظَى مِنْهَا بِالْوَجْهِ الْجَمِيلِ وَيَرْضَى عَلَيْكَ الرَّبُّ الْجَلِيلُ
sentences.tr: fa-innahā lā naẓīra lahā fī qāṣī al-arḍi wa-dānīhā wa-taḥẓā minhā bi-al-wajhi al-jamīli wa-yarḍā ʿalayka al-rabbu al-jalīlu
sentences.l: For she has no equal in the far of the earth and its near; and you will enjoy-the-favour from her of the beautiful face, and the Lord the Majestic will be pleased with you.
sentences.i: For she has no equal anywhere on earth, far or near. You will win her lovely face, and the Lord in His majesty will be pleased with you.
sentences.n: ḥaẓiya bi- is “to gain, enjoy (something)”: bi- marks the prize. raḍiya ʿalā for Classical raḍiya ʿan, “be pleased with”, is the colloquial preposition. Rhymed: al-jamīl / al-jalīl. The print runs lā and naẓīra together.

sentences.t: فَقَدْ وَرَدَ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ لَارَهْبَانِيَّةَ فِى الْإِسْلَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-qad warada ʿani al-nabiyyi ṣallā allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallama annahu qāla lā rahbāniyyata fī al-islāmi
sentences.l: For it has come down from the Prophet, God bless him and give him peace, that he said: No monkery in Islam.
sentences.i: For it has come down to us from the Prophet, God bless him and give him peace, that he said, ‘There is no monasticism in Islam.’”
sentences.n: A well-known saying: celibacy has no merit in Islam. The shadda in rahbāniyya is the print's; it runs lā and the noun together.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ تَوَجَّهَ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ كَمَالُ الْفَرَحِ وَاتَّسَعَ صَدْرُهُ وَانْشَرَحَ وَزَالَ عَنْهُ الْهَمُّ وَالْغَمُّ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika tawajjaha ilā al-maliki kamālu al-faraḥi wa-ittasaʿa ṣadruhu wa-insharaḥa wa-zāla ʿanhu al-hammu wa-al-ghammu
sentences.l: And at that, there turned towards the king the fullness of joy, and his breast widened and opened, and there departed from him the care and the grief.
sentences.i: At that the king's joy was complete; his heart grew light and glad, and all his care and sorrow left him.
sentences.n: The opposite of the narrow breast he complained of: ittasaʿa ṣadruhu wa-insharaḥa, “his breast widened and opened”. Rhymed: al-faraḥ / insharaḥa.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَ عَلَى الْوَزِيرِ وَقَالَ لَهُ اعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْوَزِيرُ أَنَّهُ لَايَتَوَجَّهُ إِلَى هَذَا الْأَمْرِ إِلَّا أَنْتَ لِكَمَالِ عَقْلِكَ وَأَدَبِكَ
sentences.tr: thumma aqbala ʿalā al-wazīri wa-qāla lahu iʿlam ayyuhā al-wazīru annahu lā yatawajjahu ilā hādhā al-amri illā anta li-kamāli ʿaqlika wa-adabika
sentences.l: Then he turned-to the vizier and said to him: Know, O vizier, that none sets-out to this matter except you, for the fullness of your intelligence and your manners.
sentences.i: Then he turned to the vizier and said, “Know, vizier, that no one shall go on this errand but you, for your understanding and your breeding are without fault.
sentences.n: li-, “for, because of”. The print runs lā and the verb together.

sentences.t: فَقُمْ إِلَى مَنْزِلِكَ وَاقْضِ أَشْغَالَكَ وَتَجَهَّزْ فِي غَدٍ وَاخْطُبْ لِي هَذِهِ الْبِنْتَ الَّتِي أَشْغَلْتَ بِهَا خَاطِرِى وَلَاتَعُدْ إِلَيَّ إِلَّابِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qum ilā manzilika wa-iqḍi ashghālaka wa-tajahhaz fī ghadin wa-ukhṭub lī hādhihi al-binta allatī ashghalta bihā khāṭirī wa-lā taʿud ilayya illā bihā
sentences.l: So rise to your dwelling and finish your affairs, and make-ready tomorrow, and ask-in-marriage for me this girl with whom you have occupied my mind; and do not return to me except with her.
sentences.i: Go home and settle your affairs, make ready tomorrow, and ask for me the hand of this girl you have set my mind on; and do not come back to me without her.”
sentences.n: ashghalta bihā khāṭirī, “you have busied my mind with her”: bi- marks what fills it. The marks on taʿud and the shaddas on ilayya and illā are the print's; it runs lā taʿud and illā bihā together.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: And he said: Hearing and obedience.
sentences.i: “With hearing and obedience,” he said.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْوَزِيرَ تَوَجَّهَ إِلَى مَنْزِلِهِ وَاسْتَدْعَى بِالْهَدَايَا الَّتِي تَصْلُحُ لِلْمُلُوكِ مِنَ الْجَوَاهِرِ وَنَفِيسِ الذَّخَائِرِ وَغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا هُوَ خَفِيفٌ فِى الْحَمْلِ ثَقِيلٌ فِى الثَّمَنِ وَمِنَ الْخَيْلِ الْعَرَبِيَّةِ وَالدُّرُوعِ الدَّاؤُدِيَّةِ وَصَنَادِيقِ الْمَالِ الَّتِي يَعْجِزُ عَنْ وَصْفِهَا الْمَقَالُ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-wazīra tawajjaha ilā manzilihi wa-istadʿā bi-al-hadāyā allatī taṣluḥu li-al-mulūki mina al-jawāhiri wa-nafīsi al-dhakhāʾiri wa-ghayri dhālika mimmā huwa khafīfun fī al-ḥamli thaqīlun fī al-thamani wa-mina al-khayli al-ʿarabiyyati wa-al-durūʿi al-dāwudiyyati wa-ṣanādīqi al-māli allatī yaʿjizu ʿan waṣfihā al-maqālu
sentences.l: Then the vizier went to his dwelling and called-for the gifts that are fit for kings: of the jewels and the precious of treasures, and other than that, of what is light in the carrying, heavy in the price; and of the Arab horses, and the Davidic coats-of-mail, and chests of wealth that speech fails from describing.
sentences.i: Then the vizier went home and sent for gifts fit for kings: jewels, precious treasures and the like, light to carry and heavy in price, Arab horses, coats of mail of David's make, and chests of money past all telling.
sentences.n: istadʿā bi- is “send for, call for (something)”: bi- marks what is fetched. David was the armourer of legend (Qurʾan 21:80), so the best mail is “Davidic”; the print spells it with a seated hamza and a shadda. “Light to carry, heavy in price” is a fixed phrase for portable riches.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ حَمَلُوهَا عَلَى الْبِغَالِ وَالْجِمَالِ وَتَوَجَّهَ الْوَزِيرُ وَمَعَهُ مِائَةُ مَمْلُوكٍ وَمِائَةُ عَبْدٍ وَمِائَةُ جَارِيَةٍ وَانْتَشَرَتْ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ الرَّايَاتُ وَالْأَعْلَامُ
sentences.tr: thumma ḥamalūhā ʿalā al-bighāli wa-al-jimāli wa-tawajjaha al-wazīru wa-maʿahu miʾatu mamlūkin wa-miʾatu ʿabdin wa-miʾatu jāriyatin wa-intasharat ʿalā raʾsihi al-rāyātu wa-al-aʿlāmu
sentences.l: Then they loaded them on the mules and the camels, and the vizier set-out, and with him a hundred mamluks and a hundred slaves and a hundred slave-girls, and there were spread over his head the banners and the flags.
sentences.i: They loaded it all on mules and camels, and the vizier set out with a hundred mamluks, a hundred slaves and a hundred slave girls, with banners and standards unfurled above his head.
sentences.n: mamlūk, “owned”, is a slave trained as a soldier or page, as against ʿabd, a plain slave.

sentences.t: وَأَوْصَاهُ الْمَلِكُ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ إِلَيْهِ فِي مُدَّةٍ قَلِيلَةٍ مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ
sentences.tr: wa-awṣāhu al-maliku an yaʾtiya ilayhi fī muddatin qalīlatin mina al-ayyāmi
sentences.l: And the king charged him that he come (back) to him in a period few of days.
sentences.i: The king charged him to come back to him within a few days.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ تَوَجُّهِهِ صَارَ الْمَلِكُ سُلَيْمَانُ شَاهْ عَلَى مَقَالِى النَّارِ مَشْغُولًا بِحُبِّهَا فِي اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda tawajjuhihi ṣāra al-maliku sulaymānu shāh ʿalā maqālī al-nāri mashghūlan bi-ḥubbihā fī al-layli wa-al-nahāri
sentences.l: And after his setting-out, King Sulaymān Shāh became (as if) on the frying-pans of the fire, occupied with love of her in the night and the day.
sentences.i: Once he had gone, King Sulaymān Shāh was as if on hot coals, taken up night and day with love for her.
sentences.n: maqālī al-nār, “the frying-pans of the fire” (pl. of miqlāh, printed with ى), is a picture of restless impatience. bi-, “with”: what keeps him busy. Rhymed: al-nār / al-nahār.

sentences.t: وَسَارَ الْوَزِيرُ لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا يَطْوِي بَرَارِيَ وَقِفَارًا حَتَّى بَقِيَ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ الْمَدِينَةِ الَّتِي هُوَ مُتَوَجِّهٌ إِلَيْهَا يَوْمٌ وَاحِدٌ
sentences.tr: wa-sāra al-wazīru laylan wa-nahāran yaṭwī barāriya wa-qifāran ḥattā baqiya baynahu wa-bayna al-madīnati allatī huwa mutawajjihun ilayhā yawmun wāḥidun
sentences.l: And the vizier journeyed night and day, folding-up wildernesses and wastes, until there remained between him and the city which he was heading to one day.
sentences.i: The vizier travelled night and day, crossing wilderness and waste, until only one day's journey lay between him and the city he was making for.
sentences.n: ṭawā, “to fold up”, of a road is to cover it fast, as if rolling it up behind one. Rhymed: nahāran / qifāran.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَزَلَ عَلَى شَاطِئِ نَهْرٍ وَأَحْضَرَ بَعْضَ خَوَاصِّهِ وَأَمَرَهُ أَنْ يَتَوَجَّهَ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ زَهْرْشَاه بِسُرْعَةٍ وَيُخْبِرَهُ بِقُدُومِهِ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: thumma nazala ʿalā shāṭiʾi nahrin wa-aḥḍara baʿḍa khawāṣṣihi wa-amarahu an yatawajjaha ilā al-maliki zahrshāh bi-surʿatin wa-yukhbirahu bi-qudūmihi ʿalayhi
sentences.l: Then he halted on the bank of a river, and brought one of his intimates and ordered him that he go to King Zahrshāh with speed and inform him of his coming to him.
sentences.i: Then he made camp on a river bank, summoned one of his closest men, and ordered him to ride quickly to King Zahrshāh and tell him of his coming.
sentences.n: bi-surʿatin, “with speed”: bi- of manner. akhbara bi- is “inform of”: bi- marks the news.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: And he said: Hearing and obedience.
sentences.i: “With hearing and obedience,” said the man.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَوَجَّهَ بِسُرْعَةٍ إِلَى تِلْكَ الْمَدِينَةِ فَلَمَّا قَدِمَ عَلَيْهَا وَافَقَ قُدُومُهُ أَنَّ الْمَلِكَ زَهْرْ شَاه كَانَ جَالِسًا فِي بَعْضِ الْمُنْتَزَهَاتِ قُدَّامَ بَابِ الْمَدِينَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma tawajjaha bi-surʿatin ilā tilka al-madīnati fa-lammā qadima ʿalayhā wāfaqa qudūmuhu anna al-malika zahr shāh kāna jālisan fī baʿḍi al-muntazahāti quddāma bābi al-madīnati
sentences.l: Then he set-out with speed to that city; and when he came upon it, his coming coincided (with) that King Zahrshāh was sitting in one of the pleasure-grounds before the gate of the city.
sentences.i: He set off at speed for the city, and it so happened that when he arrived King Zahrshāh was sitting in one of the pleasure gardens outside the city gate.
sentences.n: The king's name is broken across the printed line here, زهر / شاه.

sentences.t: فَرَآهُ وَهُوَ دَاخِلٌ وَعَرَفَ أَنَّهُ غَرِيبٌ فَأَمَرَ بِإِحْضَارِهِ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-raʾāhu wa-huwa dākhilun wa-ʿarafa annahu gharībun fa-amara bi-iḥḍārihi bayna yadayhi
sentences.l: And he saw him while he (was) entering, and knew that he (was) a stranger, and ordered his being-brought between his two hands.
sentences.i: He saw the man coming in, knew him for a stranger, and had him brought before him.
sentences.n: amara bi- is “give orders for”: bi- marks what is ordered.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا حَضَرَ الرَّسُولُ أَخْبَرَهُ بِقُدُومِ وَزِيرِ الْمَلِكِ الْأَعْظَمِ سُلَيْمَانَ شَاهْ صَاحِبِ الْأَرْضِ الْخَضْرَاءِ وَجِبَالِ أَصْفَهَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ḥaḍara al-rasūlu akhbarahu bi-qudūmi wazīri al-maliki al-aʿẓami sulaymāna shāh ṣāḥibi al-arḍi al-khaḍrāʾi wa-jibāli aṣfahāna
sentences.l: And when the messenger was present, he informed him of the coming of the vizier of the king the greatest, Sulaymān Shāh, lord of the Green Land and the mountains of Iṣfahān.
sentences.i: When the messenger stood before him he told him that the vizier of the mighty King Sulaymān Shāh, lord of the Green Land and the mountains of Iṣfahān, was on his way.
sentences.n: Iṣfahān here; the story's opening spelled it Iṣbahān. Both forms of the name are old.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ الْمَلِكُ زَهْرْشَاه وَرَحَّبَ بِالرَّسُولِ وَأَخَذَهُ وَتَوَجَّهَ إِلَى قَصْرِهِ وَقَالَ أَيْنَ فَارَقْتَ الْوَزِيرَ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa al-maliku zahrshāh wa-raḥḥaba bi-al-rasūli wa-akhadhahu wa-tawajjaha ilā qaṣrihi wa-qāla ayna fāraqta al-wazīra
sentences.l: And King Zahrshāh rejoiced and welcomed the messenger, and took him and went to his palace, and said: Where did you part-from the vizier?
sentences.i: King Zahrshāh was glad; he welcomed the messenger, took him with him to his palace, and asked, “Where did you leave the vizier?”
sentences.n: raḥḥaba bi- is “welcome (someone)”: the verb takes its object with bi-.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ فَارَقْتُهُ فِي أَوَّلِ النَّهَارِ عَلَى شَاطِئِ النَّهْرِ الْفُلَانِيِّ وَفِي غَدٍ يَكُونُ وَاصِلًا إِلَيْكَ أَدَامَ اللَّهُ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكَ وَرَحِمَ وَالِدَيْكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla fāraqtuhu fī awwali al-nahāri ʿalā shāṭiʾi al-nahri al-fulāniyyi wa-fī ghadin yakūnu wāṣilan ilayka adāma allāhu niʿmatahu ʿalayka wa-raḥima wālidayka
sentences.l: And he said: I parted-from him at the first of the day on the bank of the river so-and-so, and tomorrow he will be arriving to you — may God make-last His favour upon you and have mercy on your two parents.
sentences.i: He said, “I left him early this morning on the bank of such-and-such a river, and tomorrow he will be with you — may God keep His blessings upon you and have mercy on your parents.”
sentences.n: al-nahr al-fulānī, “the so-and-so river”: the storyteller does not trouble to name it. Rhymed: ilayka / ʿalayka / wālidayka.

sentences.t: فَأَمَرَ زَهْرْشَاه بَعْضَ وُزَرَائِهِ أَنْ يَأْخُذَ مُعْظَمَ خَوَاصِّهِ وَحُجَّابِهِ وَنُوَّابِهِ وَأَرْبَابِ دَوْلَتِهِ وَيَخْرُجَ بِهِمْ إِلَى مُقَابَلَتِهِ تَعْظِيمًا لِلْمَلِكِ سُلَيْمَانَ شَاهْ لِأَنَّ حُكْمَهُ نَافِذٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ
sentences.tr: fa-amara zahrshāh baʿḍa wuzarāʾihi an yaʾkhudha muʿẓama khawāṣṣihi wa-ḥujjābihi wa-nuwwābihi wa-arbābi dawlatihi wa-yakhruja bihim ilā muqābalatihi taʿẓīman li-al-maliki sulaymāna shāh li-anna ḥukmahu nāfidhun fī al-arḍi
sentences.l: And Zahrshāh ordered one of his viziers that he take most of his intimates and his chamberlains and his deputies and the lords of his state, and go-out with them to meet him, in honouring of King Sulaymān Shāh, because his rule (is) effective in the earth.
sentences.i: Zahrshāh ordered one of his viziers to take most of his closest men, his chamberlains, his deputies and the great officers of state, and ride out with them to meet the vizier, in honour of King Sulaymān Shāh, whose rule was felt throughout the earth.
sentences.n: arbāb al-dawla, “lords of the state”, are the officers of the court. kharaja bi-, “go out with” (bi- of accompaniment, “taking them along”).

sentences.t: هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ زَهْرْشَاه
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amri zahrshāh
sentences.l: This (is) what was of the affair of Zahrshāh.
sentences.i: So much for Zahrshāh.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْوَزِيرِ فَإِنَّهُ اسْتَقَرَّ فِي مَكَانِهِ إِلَي نِصْفِ اللَّيْلِ ثُمَّ رَحَلَ مُتَوَجِّهًا إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri al-wazīri fa-innahu istaqarra fī makānihi ilā niṣfi al-layli thumma raḥala mutawajjihan ilā al-madīnati
sentences.l: And as for what was of the affair of the vizier, he settled in his place until the middle of the night, then departed heading to the city.
sentences.i: As for the vizier, he stayed where he was until midnight and then broke camp and made for the city.
sentences.n: The print spells ilā with ي for final ى here.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا لَاحَ الصَّبَاحُ وَأَشْرَقَتِ الشَّمْسُ عَلَى الرَّوَابِي وَالْبِطَاحِ لَمْ يَشْعُرْ إِلَّا وَوَزِيرُ الْمَلِكِ زَهْرْشَاه وَحُجَّابُهُ وَأَرْبَابُ دَوْلَتِهِ وَخَوَاصُّ مَمْلَكَتِهِ قَدِمُوا عَلَيْهِ وَاجْتَمَعُوا بِهِ عَلَى فَرَاسِخَ مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā lāḥa al-ṣabāḥu wa-ashraqati al-shamsu ʿalā al-rawābī wa-al-biṭāḥi lam yashʿur illā wa-wazīru al-maliki zahrshāh wa-ḥujjābuhu wa-arbābu dawlatihi wa-khawāṣṣu mamlakatihi qadimū ʿalayhi wa-ijtamaʿū bihi ʿalā farāsikha mina al-madīnati
sentences.l: And when the morning gleamed and the sun shone on the hills and the plains, he did not perceive except (that) the vizier of King Zahrshāh and his chamberlains and the lords of his state and the intimates of his kingdom had come to him and met with him some parasangs from the city.
sentences.i: When morning broke and the sun shone on hill and plain, before he knew it King Zahrshāh's vizier, with his chamberlains, the great officers of state and the chief men of the kingdom, had come up and met him some leagues from the city.
sentences.n: lam yashʿur illā wa-, “he did not perceive but that …”, is the storyteller's “before he knew it”. A parasang (farsakh) is about three miles. Rhymed: al-ṣabāḥ / al-biṭāḥ.

sentences.t: فَأَيْقَنَ الْوَزِيرُ بِقَضَاءِ حَاجَتِهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ قَابَلُوهُ وَلَمْ يَزَالُوا سَائِرِينَ قُدَّامَهُ حَتَّى وَصَلُوا إِلَى قَصْرِ الْمَلِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-ayqana al-wazīru bi-qaḍāʾi ḥājatihi wa-sallama ʿalā alladhīna qābalūhu wa-lam yazālū sāʾirīna quddāmahu ḥattā waṣalū ilā qaṣri al-maliki
sentences.l: And the vizier became-certain of the fulfilment of his need, and greeted those who met him; and they did not cease going before him until they reached the palace of the king.
sentences.i: The vizier was sure now that his errand would succeed. He greeted those who had come to meet him, and they rode ahead of him all the way to the king's palace.
sentences.n: ayqana bi- is “be certain of”: the verb takes its object with bi-.

sentences.t: وَدَخَلُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ فِي بَابِ الْقَصْرِ إِلَى سَابِعِ دِهْلِيزٍ وَهُوَ الْمَكَانُ الَّذِي لَا يَدْخُلُهُ الرَّاكِبُ لِأَنَّهُ قَرِيبٌ مِنَ الْمَلِكِ
sentences.tr: wa-dakhalū bayna yadayhi fī bābi al-qaṣri ilā sābiʿi dihlīzin wa-huwa al-makānu alladhī lā yadkhuluhu al-rākibu li-annahu qarībun mina al-maliki
sentences.l: And they entered between his two hands in the gate of the palace to the seventh passage, and it (is) the place which the rider does not enter, because it (is) near to the king.
sentences.i: They went in before him through the palace gate as far as the seventh passageway, the place no one may enter on horseback because it is close to the king.
sentences.n: bayna yadayhi, “between his hands”, here means going ahead of him. A dihlīz is a covered entrance-passage.

sentences.t: فَتَرَجَّلَ الْوَزِيرُ وَسَعَى عَلَى قَدَمَيْهِ حَتَّى وَصَلَ إِلَى إِيوَانٍ عَالٍ
sentences.tr: fa-tarajjala al-wazīru wa-saʿā ʿalā qadamayhi ḥattā waṣala ilā īwānin ʿālin
sentences.l: And the vizier dismounted and went on his two feet until he reached a hall high.
sentences.i: The vizier dismounted and went on foot until he came to a lofty hall.
sentences.n: An īwān is a great vaulted hall open at one end, where a ruler held audience.

sentences.t: وَفِي صَدْرِ ذَلِكَ الْإِيوَانِ سَرِيرٌ مِنَ الْمَرْمَرِ مُرَصَّعٌ بِالدُّرِّ وَالْجَوْهَرِ وَلَهُ أَرْبَعَةُ قَوَائِمَ مِنْ أَنْيَابِ الْفِيلِ وَعَلَى ذَلِكَ السَّرِيرِ مَرْتَبَةٌ مِنَ الْأَطْلَسِ الْأَخْضَرِ مُطَرَّزَةٌ بِالذَّهَبِ الْأَحْمَرِ وَمِنْ فَوْقِهَا سُرَادِقٌ مُرَصَّعٌ بِالدُّرِّ وَالْجَوْهَرِ
sentences.tr: wa-fī ṣadri dhālika al-īwāni sarīrun mina al-marmari muraṣṣaʿun bi-al-durri wa-al-jawhari wa-lahu arbaʿatu qawāʾima min anyābi al-fīli wa-ʿalā dhālika al-sarīri martabatun mina al-aṭlasi al-akhḍari muṭarrazatun bi-al-dhahabi al-aḥmari wa-min fawqihā surādiqun muraṣṣaʿun bi-al-durri wa-al-jawhari
sentences.l: And in the breast of that hall (was) a throne of marble, studded with pearl and gem, and it had four legs of the tusks of the elephant; and on that throne a cushion of the satin the green, embroidered with the gold the red, and above it a canopy studded with pearl and gem.
sentences.i: At the head of the hall stood a marble throne set with pearls and jewels, on four legs of elephant ivory. On the throne lay a cushion of green satin embroidered in red gold, and over it hung a canopy set with pearls and jewels.
sentences.n: The print has يالدر, a misprint for بالدر (bi-al-durr, “with pearls”), corrected here. bi-, “with”: it marks what the throne is set with. “Red gold” is pure gold, the usual epithet. ṣadr, “breast”, of a hall is its place of honour, at the far end.

sentences.t: وَالْمَلِكُ زَهْرْشَاه جَالِسٌ عَلَى ذَلِكَ السَّرِيرِ وَأَرْبَابُ دَوْلَتِهِ وَاقِفُونَ فِي خِدْمَتِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-maliku zahrshāh jālisun ʿalā dhālika al-sarīri wa-arbābu dawlatihi wāqifūna fī khidmatihi
sentences.l: And King Zahrshāh (was) sitting on that throne, and the lords of his state standing in his service.
sentences.i: King Zahrshāh sat on that throne, with the great officers of his state standing in attendance.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ الْوَزِيرُ عَلَيْهِ وَصَارَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ ثَبَّتَ جَنَانَهُ وَأَطْلَقَ لِسَانَهُ وَأَبْدَى فَصَاحَةَ الْوُزَرَاءِ وَتَكَلَّمَ بِكَلَامِ الْبُلَغَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhala al-wazīru ʿalayhi wa-ṣāra bayna yadayhi thabbata janānahu wa-aṭlaqa lisānahu wa-abdā faṣāḥata al-wuzarāʾi wa-takallama bi-kalāmi al-bulaghāʾi
sentences.l: And when the vizier entered upon him and came between his two hands, he made-firm his heart and let-loose his tongue, and showed the eloquence of viziers, and spoke with the speech of the eloquent.
sentences.i: When the vizier came in and stood before him, he steadied his heart and loosed his tongue, and with all a vizier's eloquence he spoke as the masters of speech speak.
sentences.n: Rhymed pairs: janānahu / lisānahu, al-wuzarāʾ / al-bulaghāʾ. The night breaks off before his speech.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
